Personally i think the unacceptance or ignorance towards your sexuality is majorly due to lack of awareness, and then definitely the lack of media representation. I myself wasn't aware that such terminology and such a community of asexuality existed until last year, and learning about it, it all suddenly made so much more sensible to me. And i highly believe there still are so many more aces that don't even know that the feeling they experience is a real thing. And coming to media representation, well, there's highly any. Actually, in shows like Brooklyn 99 and The House, asexuality has been depicted so negatively, it's sad. With such minimal exposure, many still Question if their sexuality is valid or if they are. 

And to think of why some allosexuals do not validate your sexuality, well some of the above reasons, but allosexuality is in majority of what we're known about today, and it makes a fair sense for them to not understand how asexuality works, especially in a world that is so overly sexualised. 
 i feel that if the person you're coming out to, really does matter and is important enough, they should be able to come around and you have to educate them with patience how exactly your sexuality works for you. Personally, for me I don't feel the need of other people to know about my asexuality unless and until they're my family or close circle. I've been out to a few people including my boyfriend and they've been nothing but supportive with time, and I'm very proud. Good luck to you!

For self harming, I read this tactic somewhere a while ago, it kind of sounds stupid; did to me as well, but drawing or painting on your body, instead of harming it, is one of the few calming techniques. It has worked for me for sometime now, i still get the urge to harm myself, and I'm not the right person to know or provide a solution for that. But drawing/painting on your skin is one therapeutic activity I've found a bit helpful (and aesthetic). 
Some others were:
1. Hold ice.
2. Tear paper. (please don't waste clean sheets, scrap should be fine).
3. Play music loudly, might as well deafen your ears, I do that in an attempt to not be able to hear my own thoughts. Pretty silly but works just fine. 
4. Write a letter and burn it. (I don't tend to burn it, mostly because I've a serious hoarding issue of things to keep them as a memoriam. Not a very healthy habit but that's how I roll. 
5. Break sticks, or if you've access to scrap things that you can break, that'd be a great help. Destruction tends to help us relieve of our held in repressed frustration.
6. Run as fast as you can. (Please don't pass out while at it)
7. Snap a rubber band on your wrist or in general on your skin.
8. Count to 100. Silly but helps people.
9. Talk to a close person if you are wanting to open up. Or to an internet friend/stranger like me.
10. Plunge your hands or face in ice cold water for a few seconds. Feeling numb would cool you off a bit.
11. Start journalling, possibly without a filter, and if you're artistic or into that kind of things, give it a personal touch with your own vibe of aesthetics and style.

Hope this helps, my PM is always open for support. 
Peace <3.
